title.label: Title
title.help: A single line at the top of the card; what doesn't fit gets an ellipsis. Empty becomes "Notification".

subtitle.label: Subtitle
subtitle.help: Explanation under the title, across multiple lines; a line break is fine. Empty is fine.

icon.label: Icon
icon.help: A name from the list, also as mdi:name or as a hex codepoint (F12E6). Unknown or empty gives the warning triangle.

color.label: Color
color.help: One of the nine pastel colors of the tiles. Empty gives the white card.

button_text.label: Button text
button_text.help: The text on the button. Empty is "OK".

timeout.label: Timeout
timeout.help: Seconds after which the card disappears on its own. 0 waits for the button, however long that takes. The button always closes it immediately, even with a timeout.

flash.label: Blinking
flash.help: On makes the backlight blink four times when the alert arrives; the screen then just stays on.

camera.label: Camera
camera.help: A camera or image entity. Every screen but the CYD, with firmware 0.2.57+, shows its picture of that moment on the card, in the proportions of the camera itself (above the words, or beside them on a wide, low screen); a tap on it opens the camera full screen. The CYD shows the alert without it. Only through the esp_screens_show_alert event.

action.label: Action
action.help: A Home Assistant action, such as script.open_gate or light.turn_off, performed once when the button is pressed on any screen. `data` gives its fields (entity_id, brightness, ...). A timeout or a new alert leaves it unperformed. Only through the esp_screens_show_alert event.

screen.label: Screen
screen.help: Which screen gets the alert: its device name (such as kitchen-screen), the name Home Assistant shows, or a room, which reaches every screen in it. A list, such as [kitchen-screen, hallway], reaches several. Leave it out for every screen. A name that matches no screen sends nothing; the ESP Screen Manager log names the screens it knows. Only through the esp_screens_show_alert and esp_screens_dismiss_alert events.

firmware.title: Build and install screen firmware
firmware.intro: The built-in ESPHome CLI uses your own profile (YAML with keys) and secrets. Choose the screen's profile, then a USB port (screen connected to the Home Assistant machine), {ota} with the hostname, or {download} to put the firmware on the screen from your own computer. {check} only validates, {build} compiles, {install} puts the firmware on the screen. Your tiles stay as they are in ESP Screens. The first build takes a few minutes.

wifi.ready: Wi-Fi comes from your ESPHome secrets.yaml.
wifi.invalid: secrets.yaml in the ESPHome folder isn't valid YAML. Fix the file first; it won't be overwritten.

target.usb: Connect the screen with a USB data cable to the Home Assistant machine; the list refreshes on its own. Or choose Download to use your own computer.
target.download: Download the firmware and put it on the screen from your own computer, in Chrome or Edge. After that, updates go over Wi-Fi.
target.later: The profile goes into the ESPHome folder. You can install later via Firmware & USB, or from ESPHome Device Builder.
target.several: More than one board connected: choose this screen's port.
target.once: Once over USB; after that, everything is wireless.

installer.busy: A build or installation is already running ({file}). Wait for it to finish.
installer.no_cli: The ESPHome CLI is missing from this installation; only saving the profile is possible.

detail.saved: Install it later from Firmware & USB: choose this profile, then the USB port of the Home Assistant machine, or Download to put the firmware on the screen from your own computer. Save the API key for pairing:
detail.uploading: Don't disconnect the USB cable yet.
detail.building: A first build takes a few minutes on a Raspberry Pi. You can leave this page: the installation keeps running and you'll find it again under New screen.
detail.building_download: A first build takes a few minutes on a Raspberry Pi. You can leave this page: the build keeps running and you'll find it again under New screen.
detail.downloaded: Put it on the screen from your own computer, then pair the screen with Home Assistant.
detail.booted: The screen boots up and connects to your Wi-Fi. Pair it with Home Assistant now:
detail.booted_calibrate: The screen boots up and connects to your Wi-Fi. It first asks for a touch calibration: tap the crosshairs. Pair it with Home Assistant now:

download_steps.plug_bold: Plug the screen into your computer
download_steps.open: {bold} in Chrome or Edge, click Connect and choose the screen's USB port.
download_steps.install: {bold} and select {file}. The screen restarts and joins your Wi-Fi.
download_steps.install_calibrate: {bold} and select {file}. The screen restarts and joins your Wi-Fi. It first asks for a touch calibration: tap the crosshairs.

installer.download_keep: The file holds your Wi-Fi password and the screen's keys: keep it to yourself.

pairing.ha: {bold} This happens outside ESP Screens. Home Assistant discovers {name} as an ESPHome device; click Add. Not discovered? Add ESPHome manually with the screen's IP address.
pairing.ha_bold: Go to Home Assistant → Settings → Devices & services.
pairing.key: {bold} above when Home Assistant asks for an encryption key.
pairing.actions: {bold} ESPHome integration → Configure → “Allow the device to perform Home Assistant actions”. Without this, the screen sees everything but controls nothing.
pairing.tiles: {bold} Back in ESP Screens, the screen appears in the list on the left within about thirty seconds; until then it's shown there as “not yet in Home Assistant”.

alerts.title: A full-screen notification, from an automation.
alerts.intro: Every screen has the {action} action. It places a card over everything, wakes the screen, and keeps the backlight at normal brightness until someone taps the button or the timeout runs out. Home Assistant itself shows no explanation or dropdowns for ESPHome actions; everything you can fill in is listed here.
alerts.loading: The cheatsheet is still loading; one moment.

try.text: Send one alert now, with the same fields an automation sends. The screen shows the card and, with blinking on, flashes its backlight.
try.title: Title
try.subtitle: Subtitle
try.flash_hint: Four times when the alert arrives.
try.sent_all: Sent to {n} screen. | Sent to {n} screens.
try.skipped: 1 skipped (offline or old firmware). | {n} skipped (offline or old firmware).
try.nothing: No screen could show it: check that a screen is online with firmware {version} or newer.

screens.text: Every screen has its own action, with the device name in it. From firmware {version}; update an older screen with its Update button under Screens.
screens.none: No screen paired yet. Install one via New screen; the action appears once Home Assistant sees the screen.
screens.unknown: Device name unknown · update the screen

howto.add: {add} and search for {esphome}. Choose your screen's action: Home Assistant calls it "Performs the action show_alert of the node {device}".
howto.fields: {bold} Home Assistant asks for all seven; leave what you don't use empty ({empty}, {zero}, off).
howto.yaml: Prefer YAML? Choose {edit} on the action and paste the example below.

all.title: All screens at once
all.text: Fire the event {show} with the same fields, and ESP Screens passes the alert on to every screen that is online, including screens you add later. {dismiss} clears it everywhere. In an automation, add the {event} action or paste the example under {edit}. Leave out the fields you don't use. ESP Screens has to be running for this.

fields.text: Text is free-form; the limit is in bytes, and an accented letter counts as two. What doesn't fit gets an ellipsis (title) or is dropped (subtitle).
fields.camera_limit: Every screen but the CYD, firmware 0.2.57+

icons.text: Fill in the name in {field}, for example {example}. {mdi} and the hex codepoint ({hex}) also work. Only these icons are included in the firmware; any other name shows the warning triangle. Tap an icon to copy its name.
icons.extra: Also available: control and weather icons
icons.none: No icon for "{query}". Unknown names show the warning triangle ({fallback}).

colors.text: Fill in the name in {field}. These are the pastel shades of the tiles, with dark text. Empty or unknown gives the white card. Tap to copy.

behaviour.wakes: {bold} An alert immediately wakes a dimmed or dark screen and appears above every page, every open light card, and the standby layer.
behaviour.on: {bold} As long as the card is showing, the backlight stays at normal brightness. Standby and night hours wait. After the button, the regular standby time starts again.
behaviour.timeout: {bold} {zero} waits for the button, however long that takes. With {minute} the card disappears after a minute, but the button closes it sooner.
behaviour.blinking: {bold} {flash} blinks the backlight four times when the alert arrives (about a second) and leaves the screen on afterward.
behaviour.replacing: {bold} A new alert replaces the current one; there's no stack. The replaced alert reports itself as {replaced}.
behaviour.closing: {bold} {dismiss} clears the card, for example if the door is already open. Without an alert, that action does nothing.
behaviour.beside: {bold} does nothing; only the button closes it. That way a wake-up tap never accidentally dismisses the alert.

events.text: Every end fires the event {event} with {action}, {title}, {screen} (the device name) and the {device_id} that Home Assistant adds. Visible under Settings → Tools → Events.
events.wait: Waiting until someone presses the button

tips.color: Use a {bold}: orange for the door, red for smoke or water, green for "done". The text always stays dark and readable.
tips.short: Keep the title {bold}; a screen shows about twenty characters on one line and ends a longer title with an ellipsis. Put details in the subtitle.
tips.button: A {bold} turns the notification into a question: "Coming", "Seen", "Turn off". The event then tells you who responded.
tips.resolve: For an alert that resolves itself (the door opens, the laundry gets taken out) close it in the same automation with {dismiss}.
tips.every: Every screen? Fire {event} once (see All screens at once). The screens still work independently and each reports with its own {screen}.
tips.claude: Rather {bold} for the automation? Install the ESP Screens skill under Settings → Claude.

wait_yaml.comment: Doorbell: show the alert and wait until someone presses the button.
wait_yaml.message: Someone is coming to the door.

one.title: One screen, with a camera or a button action
one.text: Add {screen} to the same event and only that screen gets the alert. That is how a single screen shows a {camera} picture or runs an {action} from its button: the screen's own action has no fields for those. After {screen} comes one of the values in the list below.
one.more: A few screens? Give a list, such as {list}. A room works too and reaches every screen in it. A name that matches no screen sends nothing; the ESP Screen Manager log then names the screens it knows.
one.name: Name in Home Assistant
one.picture_no: No, the alert comes without it
one.none: No screens paired yet. Once a screen is paired, what to fill in for it appears here.

override.title: Override YAML
override.intro: This small file is yours. It is loaded after the shared screen package and stays in place when ESP Screens updates. Change hardware-specific details here, such as a display model.
override.safe_text: Display, touchscreen, substitutions, pins and other device details. Name, Wi-Fi, API, OTA and package links remain managed.
override.no_profile: No ESPHome profile was found for this screen.
override.attached: Changes here apply on the next build.
override.not_attached: Save once to attach this file to the profile.
override.saved: Saved. The override is kept during firmware updates.
override.checking: Saved. ESPHome is checking the complete profile…
override.valid: The complete profile is valid. Safe to build and install.
override.rejected: ESPHome rejected the complete profile. See Firmware & USB for the full log.
override.confirm_example: Replace the current text with the example?
override.example_loaded: Example loaded. Save it when you are ready.
override.cleared: The override will be empty after you save.

preview.intro: Design a screen using Home Assistant entities without pairing hardware. Previews are saved in this browser; taps in the firmware preview control Home Assistant.
preview.design_only: Preview profile only. This does not add physical firmware support for this board.
preview.name: Preview name
preview.invalid_shape: Choose a name, a supported profile, a 1–8 column/row grid and a 160–2560 pixel canvas.
preview.remove: The preview and its saved layout in this browser.
